model_annotation: The figure is a nested (two-level) donut chart intended to show the distribution of two related categorical measures, with the outer ring representing “Ambiguity Std (Outer)” and the inner ring representing “Max Ambiguity (Inner).” The outer ring contains 4 slices, each labeled with a percentage inside the segment: a dark teal slice at about 49.0%, a slightly lighter teal/blue slice at about 39.0%, a bright cyan slice at about 7.0%, and a medium blue slice at about 5.0; the legend for this ring lists standard-deviation categories, including “Std: 0.47,” “Std: 0.82,” and “Std: 0.94,” with one additional entry present but visually obscured/blurred. The inner ring contains 3 slices with percentages shown inside: “Max: 1” in a medium light blue at about 47.7%, “Max: 2” in a lighter blue at about 38.0%, and “Max: 3” in a very pale blue at about 14.2%. Two separate legends appear on the right corresponding to the outer and inner rings, and there is no visible explosion/offset or other emphasis beyond the use of distinct blue-toned colors; visually, the segments in both rings appear arranged with the largest slices occupying the longest arcs and smaller slices grouped together on one side.
